metadata.goal: Investigate the repeated operating patterns of vessels travelling between a harbour and nearby offshore areas.
metadata.dataset_description: Forty repeated fishing voyages and twelve ferry movements near a west-Jutland harbour, including twelve synchronized fishing–ferry encounter voyages.
metadata.source_note: Danish maritime geography is used as context; the visible trajectories and attributes are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: A large share of the repeated offshore activity is generated by the same fishing vessel, whose voyages consistently connect the harbour with a compact offshore working area.

plot.title: Repeated Harbour–Offshore Activity
plot.description: Map the same vessel repeatedly following a similar harbour--offshore working-area--harbour path, with limited voyage-to-voyage variation.

insight_list.question: Who generates the repeated offshore activity?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Map the same vessel repeatedly following a similar harbour--offshore working-area--harbour path, with limited voyage-to-voyage variation.

insight_list.insight: The fishing vessel alternates between direct harbour transits and low-speed offshore operations before returning to the harbour.

plot.title: Fishing Transit and Operating Phases
plot.description: Compare voyage-progress speed profiles and successive COG changes between harbour-transit and offshore-operation phases.

insight_list.question: How does the fishing vessel alternate between transit and work?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare voyage-progress speed profiles and successive COG changes between harbour-transit and offshore-operation phases.

insight_list.insight: There are also some ferry vessels that repeatedly travel between the harbour and offshore areas, but they are less frequent and show more consistent speed and heading patterns than the fishing vessel.

plot.title: Fishing and Ferry Movement Consistency
plot.description: Compare trajectory frequency, within-voyage speed variation, and successive heading changes; heading consistency is measured from heading rather than COG.

insight_list.question: How do recurring ferry movements differ from fishing movements?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare trajectory frequency, within-voyage speed variation, and successive heading changes; heading consistency is measured from heading rather than COG.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np

insight_list.insight: When the fishing vessel approaches ferry vessels, it tends to increase speed to move away quickly and changes its status from under way fishing to under way using engine.

plot.title: Fishing-vessel Response Near Ferries
plot.description: Use a close-range view and distance-band summary to show the pronounced speed increase and engine-status transition within one kilometre of a synchronized ferry position.

insight_list.question: How does the fishing vessel respond when it approaches a ferry?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use a close-range view and distance-band summary to show the pronounced speed increase and engine-status transition within one kilometre of a synchronized ferry position.

insights: A large share of the repeated offshore activity is generated by the same fishing vessel, whose voyages consistently connect the harbour with a compact offshore working area.
The fishing vessel alternates between direct harbour transits and low-speed offshore operations before returning to the harbour.

There are also some ferry vessels that repeatedly travel between the harbour and offshore areas, but they are less frequent and show more consistent speed and heading patterns than the fishing vessel.
When the fishing vessel approaches ferry vessels, it tends to increase speed to move away quickly and changes its status from under way fishing to under way using engine.
summary: A large share of the repeated offshore activity is generated by the same fishing vessel, whose voyages consistently connect the harbour with a compact offshore working area. The fishing vessel alternates between direct harbour transits and low-speed offshore operations before returning to the harbour. There are also some ferry vessels that repeatedly travel between the harbour and offshore areas, but they are less frequent and show more consistent speed and heading patterns than the fishing vessel. When the fishing vessel approaches ferry vessels, it tends to increase speed to move away quickly and changes its status from under way fishing to under way using engine.
